Package net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.parser2

Class PrioritizedValue

java.lang.Object
net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.parser2.PrioritizedValue
public final class PrioritizedValue extends Object
One property value, together with the priority it was assigned when merged in (see MergedStyleNode.mergeRule(net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.parser2.RawStyleRule, net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.AutomaticCounter, boolean)) -- the direct counterpart of the legacy net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.DarkString, kept under the same name it had before this class grew a dark half. A property can carry a getLight() value, a getDark() one, or both: a plain declaration (outside any @media block) sets only getLight(): a declaration inside @media (prefers-color-scheme:dark) { ... } sets only getDark(). When both a light and a dark declaration reach the very same property of the very same selector, mergeWith(PrioritizedValue) folds them into ONE value carrying both -- exactly what lets the final color object (see net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.ValueImpl#asColor, HColor#withDark) embed both variants and let the actual theme be picked at render/output time (e.g. so a single generated SVG can follow the viewer's prefers-color-scheme setting), instead of one theme being baked in once and for all when the style sheet is resolved.

    mergeWith(PrioritizedValue existing)
    Merges this (incoming) value with existing (already accumulated for the same property), mirroring DarkString#mergeWith exactly: if both are the same kind (both light-only, or both dark-only) -- or either one is already a combined light+dark value -- the strictly higher priority wins outright, and on an exact tie existing wins, not the incoming value; if one is light-only and the other is dark-only, they combine into one value carrying both, keeping whichever priority belonged to the light-only side of the pair. existing may be null (nothing accumulated yet), in which case this value is returned unconditionally.

      public PrioritizedValue mergeWith(PrioritizedValue existing)
      Merges this (incoming) value with existing (already accumulated for the same property), mirroring DarkString#mergeWith exactly:
      • if both are the same kind (both light-only, or both dark-only) -- or either one is already a combined light+dark value -- the strictly higher priority wins outright, and on an exact tie existing wins, not the incoming value;
      • if one is light-only and the other is dark-only, they combine into one value carrying both, keeping whichever priority belonged to the light-only side of the pair.
      existing may be null (nothing accumulated yet), in which case this value is returned unconditionally.
